what_its_for: Oseltamivir is an antiviral medicine used to treat the flu (influenza) in people who have had symptoms for no more than 2 days. It can also be used to prevent the flu in people who have been exposed to someone with it. It works by stopping the flu virus from spreading inside your body, which helps you feel better faster and may reduce how long you are sick.
how_to_take: Take oseltamivir by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Swallow capsules whole. If you have trouble swallowing capsules, talk to your pharmacist — a liquid form is available. Take every dose as directed and finish the full course of treatment, even if you start feeling better before it is done.
dosing: For treating the flu in adults and children 13 years and older: the usual dose is 75 mg twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening) for 5 days. For preventing the flu after exposure: the usual dose is 75 mg once a day for at least 10 days. Doses are lower for young children and are based on their weight. Always follow the exact dose your doctor or pharmacist tells you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if your next scheduled dose is within 2 hours, skip the missed dose and just take the next one at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store capsules at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep them out of the bathroom. If you have the liquid suspension, store it in the refrigerator and use it within 17 days. Do not freeze the liquid. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods or drinks you must strictly avoid while taking oseltamivir. However, avoid getting the live nasal spray flu vaccine (FluMist) within 2 weeks before or 48 hours after taking oseltamivir, as it may not work as well. Always let your doctor and pharmacist know about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing); unusual behavior, confusion, hallucinations, or self-injury (these rare side effects have been reported, especially in children); severe skin reactions with blistering or peeling; or if your symptoms get much worse instead of better. Also call your doctor if you have kidney disease, since your dose may need to be adjusted.
when_it_works: Oseltamivir works best when started within 48 hours (2 days) of your first flu symptoms. Most people begin to feel some improvement within 1 to 2 days of starting treatment. It typically shortens the duration of the flu by about 1 to 2 days. It does not cure the flu instantly, so continue taking it for the full prescribed course.
special_populations: Children: Dosing is based on your child's weight and age. The liquid form is often easier for young children. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Oseltamivir is generally considered safe during pregnancy and breastfeeding when the benefits outweigh the risks — talk to your doctor. Elderly patients: Older adults can use this medicine normally, but kidney function should be checked since the dose may need to be lowered. People with kidney problems: A lower dose or less frequent dosing may be needed. Always tell your doctor if you have any kidney issues.
